wu: Students play 'Speed Review' in teams. Teacher shows flashcards of jobs (doctor, teacher, engineer). Teams race to say the job and one sentence about it (e.g., 'A doctor helps people').
wuAlt: Students do a 'Find Someone Who' survey about future jobs using 'Are you going to be...?' questions.
Teacher writes 5 job-related words on the board; students create sentences with them in 60 seconds.
pres: Teacher introduces 'Dream Job Interviews' using a model dialogue. She pretends to be a job interviewer (e.g., 'Why do you want to be a teacher?'). Elicit question forms and model answers. Check understanding with 'What question did I ask?'
presAlt: Teacher uses a short video clip of a job interview (1 min) and discusses it with the class.
Students match interview questions to possible answers (e.g., 'What are your strengths?' → 'I am hard-working').
prac: Students practice in pairs. One is the interviewer, the other is the job applicant. Teacher provides a question list (e.g., 'Why do you want this job?', 'What can you do?'). Monitor and correct errors.
pracAlt: Students play 'Interview Chain': one student asks a question, the next answers and asks a new question, etc.
Teacher distributes 'Job Role Cards' (e.g., 'You are a chef') and students prepare questions for that role.
ls: Students listen to a KET-style listening recording of a job interview. They tick the correct answers on a worksheet (multiple choice).
re: After break, students play 'Job Charades'. One student acts out a job; others guess using 'Are you a...?' questions.
prod: Students conduct a 'Dream Job Interview' in pairs. They take turns asking and answering 6 questions about their dream job. Teacher observes for fluency and accuracy.
rw: Students complete a KET-style writing task: 'Write 40-50 words about your dream job. Say what it is and why you want it.' Teacher provides a sentence starter: 'My dream job is...'
st: Teacher reads a short story about a young person achieving their dream job. End with the goodbye routine: 'Today we practiced job interviews and celebrated our progress. Thank you, class!'
g: Teams answer trivia questions about jobs (e.g., 'Where does a doctor work?')
Students describe a job without naming it (e.g., 'You wear a uniform and drive a bus')
Students write jobs on a bingo card; cross off when a classmate mentions it
Students switch partners every 2 minutes for quick interviews
Match job ads to the right person using picture cards
diff: Fast finishers: Write a short paragraph about a famous person's job.
Support: Use a word bank with job vocabulary and sentence starters.
hw: Write a dream-job interview Q&A (6 exchanges).
Review all your notes for the assessment week.
Watch a short video about a job and write 3 sentences about it.
tip: Use peer feedback during the interview practice to build confidence—students learn from each other's mistakes in a low-stakes environment.
checklist: I can ask and answer questions about jobs
I can write 40-50 words about my dream job
I can understand a short interview recording
I can use 'going to' for future plans
I can compare jobs using 'better than'
I can participate in a paired interview
